title: Copilot Studio: agent node runs an AI agent as a workflow step
summary: The briefing passes: the roadmap facts, documented behaviour, licensing qualifications and control paths are supported. Both API calls are documented, and targeted searches found no documented node-specific switch or human-assistance enforcement API.

claims.where: title; summary; What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: The agent node hands a workflow step to an AI agent that can reason.
claims.quote: The agent node lets a flow hand a step over to an AI agent that can reason, call tools, and pull from knowledge sources before returning a result.

claims.claim: The agent can call tools during the workflow step.
claims.quote: Equip the agent with tools (Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers and connectors) so it can take action.

claims.claim: The agent can read attached knowledge sources before returning its result.
claims.quote: Ground the agent in knowledge (SharePoint sites, public websites) so it can answer from your content.

claims.claim: The agent response becomes dynamic content available to subsequent workflow steps.
claims.quote: The agent response then becomes available as dynamic content that you can use in any subsequent step.

claims.claim: An existing agent is selected from a list of published agents.
claims.quote: An existing agent: Select a published agent from a list.

claims.claim: An existing agent uses its previously configured instructions, tools and knowledge.
claims.quote: The agent runs with whatever instructions, tools, and knowledge it was already configured with.

claims.claim: New agent for this workflow creates an inline agent configured inside the node.
claims.quote: New agent for this workflow: Build an inline agent scoped to this workflow.

claims.claim: The inline agent's instructions, tools, knowledge and output shape travel with the workflow.
claims.quote: The agent's instructions, tools, knowledge, and output shape are configured in the node itself and travel with the workflow.

claims.claim: An inline agent cannot be reused outside its workflow.
claims.quote: Can the inline agent be reused outside this workflow? No. An inline agent is scoped to its workflow.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls: first table row
claims.claim: The tenant-pool draw control is at Power Platform admin center > Licensing > Products > Copilot Studio > Manage Copilot Credits > environment > Capacity overages > Draw from the available capacity in my tenant.

claims.where: controls[0].api; Governance controls: first table row
claims.claim: PUT https://api.powerplatform.com/licensing/allocationsV2?api-version=2024-10-01 writes an environment allocation.
claims.quote:
$apiBaseUrl    = "https://api.powerplatform.com"
$apiVersion    = "2024-10-01"
Invoke-RestMethod -Method Put `
    -Uri "$apiBaseUrl/licensing/allocationsV2?api-version=$apiVersion"

claims.claim: The allocation request identifies Copilot Credits using allocatedEntitlements[].entitlementId set to MCSMessages.
The allocation request disables tenant-pool draw with an enforcementRules entry having ruleType TenantPool and enabled false.
claims.quote:
enforcementRules = @(
                # Disable TenantPool so the environment is capped at its allocation.
                # Set enabled = $true to let the environment draw from tenant capacity.
                @{ ruleType = "TenantPool"; enabled = $false }

claims.claim: The example payload sets scope.environmentId, an example allocation quantity of 5000 and the disabled TenantPool enforcement rule.
The allocation request requires authenticated authorization.
claims.quote:
$auth = Get-MsalToken -ClientId $clientId -TenantId $tenantId -Scope "https://api.powerplatform.com/.default" -Interactive
$headers = @{ Authorization = "Bearer $($auth.AccessToken)" }

claims.claim: The tutorial sends the allocation body with Content-Type application/json.
claims.quote: -Headers $headers -ContentType "application/json" -Body $allocationBody
